title: Betis vs. Osasuna: Decisive Clash in La Liga's 8th Round
seoTitle: Betis vs. Osasuna: La Liga's 8th Round Decisive Clash
subtitle: Sunday's classic brings together the third-placed team and the side looking to react after the FIFA international break.
excerpt: Real Betis hosts Osasuna this Sunday, the 11th, at 1:30 PM (Brasília time), at the La Cartuja stadium in Seville.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Real Betis and Osasuna, scheduled for this Sunday, the 11th, emerges as one of the highlights of La Liga's 8th round after the FIFA international break. The encounter will decide if Betis maintains its third-place position and if Osasuna can break its streak of negative results.

What's at Stake for Betis

With 16 points from seven matches, Betis holds the third position and seeks to reclaim the spot lost to Real Madrid. Manuel Pellegrini's team went into the break on a 14-game unbeaten run at home, but still needs to confirm if the pace shown before the pause will be maintained. The break was used to recover players like Marc Bartra and Diego Llorente, as well as allowing Ceballos and Lo Celso to undergo a mini pre-season.

Osasuna's Challenges After the Break

Osasuna, with eight points from seven matches, returns to competition after 22 days of inactivity. Luis Miguel Ramis's team aims to break a streak of three losses in their last four fixtures and improve their points tally, which has been below expectations. Among the absences are Aimar Oroz, who felt a muscular problem, and Kike Barja, who continues to experience discomfort.

Players Who Could Decide the Outcome

In attack, Colombian Cucho Hernández arrives at the clash with two goals and one assist this season, competing with Parrott for a spot in Betis's offense. On Osasuna's side, Croatian Ante Budimir concentrates the team's firepower, having scored five of the club's six league goals.

How to Watch the Match

The match will be played at 6:30 PM (local time) at the La Cartuja stadium in Seville, corresponding to 1:30 PM Brasília time. In Spain, the broadcast is handled by Movistar LaLiga TV. In Brazil, the match can be watched for free on the YouTube channel Cazé TV, which offers live streaming without charge.

Recent Head-to-Head History

In 84 official encounters, Betis leads with 42 wins, 16 draws, and 26 losses. When playing at home, the "Verdiblanco" won 28 of 42 matches, while Osasuna triumphed only four times. This historical advantage reinforces the expectation of an open game, where efficiency in set pieces and area management could be decisive.
